 "Title": "Alignment-adaptive residual CDF: weighting the positional correction by measured anatomy alignment",
 "Summary": "Use the residual empirical CDF (positional median subtracted, global CDF of residuals) but weight the positional correction by how much the supports' normal scores actually vary with position, so unaligned modalities fall back to the plain global CDF automatically.",
 "Hypothesis": "The alignment-adaptive residual CDF is never worse than the global empirical CDF by more than 0.3 pixel-AUROC points on any held-out dataset, and on spatially aligned datasets it keeps at least 80% of the full residual-CDF gain, at all K.",
 "Rationale": "The global-CDF parent is safe but ignores anatomy; the residual-CDF parent removes anatomy offsets but assumes alignment. Their combination measures alignment from the supports themselves: the share of variance of leave-one-out support scores explained by grid position (an intraclass correlation, rho).  "Method": "1) utils.py: rho = var_between_positions / (var_between + var_within) of LOO support scores per branch and level (positions pooled in 3x3 neighbourhoods). 2) Residual r = s_j - rho x med_j (med_j shrunk positional median); reference set built from support LOO residuals computed the same way. 3) test_few.py: F(r) via searchsorted; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed.  "Summary": "Make the residual empirical CDF strictly leave-one-out: each support's residual reference scores are computed with a positional median and a memory bank that exclude that support, so the reference distribution matches what a new test image sees.",
 "Hypothesis": "At K <= 4, the exact leave-one-out residual CDF reduces the gap between the support-derived and the realised specificity at a 95%-specificity threshold by at least 3 points relative to the non-exact residual CDF, while keeping AUROC equal within 0.5 points.",
 "Rationale": "Both parents build references from leave-one-out patch scores, but the residual variant subtracts a positional median that includes the very support whose scores form the reference. At small K this shrinks the residuals of supports relative to those of a new image, so thresholds set on supports are too low and specificity is overestimated. {
 "Title": "Augmented-support reference sets for inductive normalisation at small K",
 "Summary": "Enlarge the leave-one-out reference set of every normaliser by scoring label-preserving augmentations of the K normal supports (flips, small shifts and rotations, mild intensity jitter), so the reference distribution reflects normal variability even at K = 2.",
 "Hypothesis": "At K = 2, building the empirical-CDF reference from 16 augmentations per support reduces the standard deviation of image AUROC across support draws by at least 30% and increases mean pixel AUROC by at least 1 point over the unaugmented reference, with no benefit expected at K = 16.",
 "Rationale": "Both parents spend all their effort on how to map scores, while their common weakness is how few normal scores are available: at K = 2 the reference consists of two images scored against a one-image bank. A different lever is the reference itself. Normal anatomy varies by position, orientation and intensity; label-preserving augmentations of the supports sample this variation and give many more leave-one-out reference scores without any extra data. Augmented views are scored against the bank of the other supports only, so the scheme stays strictly inductive.",
 "Method": "1) utils.py: augment(x, n=16): horizontal flip (where anatomically valid), shifts up to 8 px, rotations up to 10 degrees, gamma in [0.8, 1.2]. 2) build_refs: for each support i and each augmented view, few-shot scores against the bank of the other supports (unaugmented) and zero-shot scores; pool into the reference arrays. 3) test_few.py: empirical CDF per branch and level; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged; test-set min-max removed. Hyper-parameters: n in {4, 16, 64}. No training.",
 "Experiment": "Leave-one-modality-out on BMAD (RESC and OCT17 held out together), MVFA retrained with source-validation selection; K in {2, 4, 8, 16}; 3 seeds x 3 support draws; 0.5 fusion and max pooling unchanged. Baselines: transductive MVFA pipeline, support percentiles (problem statement). Additional baseline: unaugmented empirical CDF. Metrics: mean and standard deviation of image/pixel AUROC across support draws per K. Falsified if variance at K = 2 is not reduced by 30%.",
 "Provenance": [
  "MadCLIP: Few-shot Medical Anomaly Detection with CLIP",
  "Beyond Static Anchors: Bounded Prototype Conditioning for Language-Free Medical Anomaly Detection"
